subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Which credential boundary should OpenClaw own for agent-executed commands and plugin operations: SecretRef migration only, a scoped broker/proxy, process or OS isolation, or a staged combination?
rationale: The remaining gap defines a security boundary, config/API surface, migration behavior, and compatibility policy that cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Stage a native broker boundary
options.body: Keep this issue open and converge the scoped broker/proxy work with SecretRef migration and exact redaction while documenting what shell/file isolation still requires.

options.title: Limit core to SecretRefs and docs
options.body: Declare SecretRefs plus existing redaction as the supported core boundary and route stronger isolation to plugins, containers, or external proxies.

options.title: Require process isolation first
options.body: Pause masked-secret config work until OpenClaw has a maintainer-approved OS/container isolation design for agent-executed tools.

recommendation.title: Stage a native broker boundary
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and converge the scoped broker/proxy work with SecretRef migration and exact redaction while documenting what shell/file isolation still requires.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the credential security boundary and CODEOWNERS routes the relevant secrets and agent auth surfaces to this owner group.
